title: Three.js Mouse Trouble Game
author: Appropriate_Sail3890
selftext:
Been working on this for 2 weeks now.

Tom and jerry loot extraction mischief is the tag line i've been working towards.

Mouse and cat are meshy low poly rigged with [https://app.mesh2motion.org/](https://app.mesh2motion.org/)

I put a sprite sheet for their eyes from Nano banana so they have some more expression.

Textures created as 100 texture atlas's from Nano Banana 2 in one generation.

The level is made of primitives with a build mode/prefab editor to place prefabs and primitives.

All loads in about 6MB from a cloudflare worker and cloudflare party kit for multiplayer support.

Mobile support as well.

Pretty much every AI touched this, Claude, Codex, Cursor

let me know what you think!

try it now: [https://mouse.ryanfitzpatrick.io](https://mouse.ryanfitzpatrick.io)

repo: [https://github.com/ryanfitzpatrickio/mouse\_vibejam2026](https://github.com/ryanfitzpatrickio/mouse_vibejam2026)

comments.author: SipHappensTea
comments.body: This is so cool! What base skillset do you need to vibe code a game like this?

replies.author: Appropriate_Sail3890
replies.body: I learned one project at a time, pile of failures and experiments to figure out each game system, been vibe coding games for a year now, since GPT 5/Claude 4.5 came out the models have stepped up a bit feels like.

replies.author: SipHappensTea
replies.body: Glad to hear it’s possible to learn as you go! Being okay with failure is pretty much a prerequisite for vibe coding. Great work!

comments.author: scottyp12345
comments.body: This looks like a fun idea. I really like those eyes you put on the mice to give them more character.

replies.author: Appropriate_Sail3890
replies.body: I know right! I'm sure it's been done before but its sooo cheap and easy to implement in threejs. I'm just going to keep doing it going forward, this style is great for velocity as I can get quick style fidelity for cheap.
